News.title: Famous TikTok star sexually assaulted on popular Spanish tourist beach before dog-walker finds her sobbing between cars
News.content:
INFLUENCER’S HORROR Famous TikTok star sexually assaulted on popular Spanish tourist beach before dog-walker finds her sobbing between cars

A FAMOUS TikTok star was sexually assaulted on a popular Spanish tourist beach, left crying her eyes out between two vehicles.

The brutal attack allegedly took place on Gandia beach, approximately 70 miles south of Valencia.





This popular tourist hotspot on the Costa de Valencia is known for its beaches and beautiful scenery.

The alleged victim is a foreign woman reportedly in her thirties, but her nationality is currently unknown.

She is known for posting content on social media and had reportedly planned to document her stay online.

Consequently, one disturbing theory is that she may have been stalked by an obsessed follower.

A resident of Grau de Gandia was walking his pet dog when he stumbled upon the distraught woman.

He reportedly heard sobbing coming from between two cars and found the victim crouched down, unable to stop crying.

He immediately called the police who rushed to the scene.

After briefly speaking with officers, she was rushed to Francesc de Boja Hospital for an examination.



In the immediate aftermath, the police began to search the area using what little information they had.

They were looking for someone matching the vague description the woman had given them.

The authorities are now looking through CCTV footage to try and identify the would-be aggressor.

While the location is a public area, it is also quite isolated and screened.

They are also inspecting the victim’s social media to see if she received any threatening messages or had even met the suspect at some point.



Investigators also interviewed the resident who was walking his pet and another woman who was on her balcony when the attack supposedly happened.

According to Spanish outlet Levante-EMV, the woman was approached by at least one stranger when she was walking down a street on Gandia beach.

The victim had been hanging out in local entertainment venues, leading others to think it may be someone she met inside.

The man then pounced and sexually assaulted her, leaving her in-between the two vehicles.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The woman has yet to give a full account of what happened due to her distressed state.



DNA samples will now be sent to the National Institute of Technology in Barcelona to see if they match anyone in their database.

News.title: Shocking moment ‘unlicensed’ pilot crashes helicopter into field seconds after takeoff with family onboard
News.content:
THIS is the heart-stopping moment a helicopter carrying a family and a young child plummeted from the sky just 15 seconds after take-off.

The Robinson R44 chopper, carrying four people including a nine-year-old boy, smashed into a field in Brazil, leaving witnesses horrified.





Incredibly, all four on board scrambled from the mangled wreckage alive, despite the aircraft sustaining massive damage.

The footage, which has since gone viral, shows the helicopter struggling during its initial climb near the luxury Garden Hotel in Campina Grande, before the engine seemingly cuts out and it drops like a stone.

Witnesses watched in shock as the chopper hit the dirt in a terrifying heap of twisted metal.

Businessman Josevan Rodrigues Ferreira, 46, was arrested by cops after investigators found he wasn’t licensed to fly the aircraft.

Police chief Rodrigo Monteiro confirmed the pilot lacked a valid flight license and his medical certificate had expired.

In a chilling twist, it has now emerged that the doomed chopper, registration PR-DCM, is essentially a ‘cursed’ machine.

Records show the aircraft had cheated death once before, having smashed into the ground 700 miles away in a separate incident back in

July 2013, with all four passengers escaping with minor injuries.



Ferreira was rushed to the Campina Grande Trauma Hospital for treatment following the crash last Saturday and was slapped in handcuffs the next day upon his discharge.

He has since been released but now faces serious charges of endangering air transport safety.

Also on board were the pilot’s twin brother, Josean, and the helicopter’s owner, businessman Lamartynne Oliveira.

Brazilian aviation authorities have now launched a full investigation into the crash.

News.title: Terrifying reign of ‘UK’s most violent poltergeist’ who dragged teen up stairs by her throat & BRANDED her with a cross
News.content:
BLACK MONK Terrifying reign of ‘UK’s most violent poltergeist’ who dragged teen up stairs by her throat & BRANDED her with a cross

WHEN Joe and Jean moved into their spacious semi in Pontefract, west Yorkshire, they were thrilled to have more room for their two children, Phillip, 15, and 12-year-old Diane.

Little did they know they were walking into their very own horror movie.





Over the next three years, the family were left traumatised by unexplained phenomena as “Britain’s most violent poltergeist” hurled objects, ripped up furniture and smashed crockery – leading one relative to declare “the devil is in that house.”

The reign of terror by the unknown entity, dubbed Mr Nobody by Jean, culminated with Diane being dragged up the stairs by her throat and BRANDED with a metal cross.

The historic case, also known as The Black Monk of Pontefract, is revisited in the latest episodes of the podcast Uncanny, hosted by Danny Robins.

Resident sceptic Dr Ciaran O’Keefe and paranormal psychologist Evelyn Hollow join the presenter to weigh up the evidence and theories surrounding the sinister tale, which begins in August 1966, when the family moved into 30 East Drive.



Knowing the family needed more space, mum Jean had arranged a swap with the previous tenants of the council house, who seemed eager to move out.

Within days it’s claimed that Phillip, at home with his grandmother, saw a thick cloud of grey-white powder hanging in the air in the lounge.

A puddle of water then appeared in the kitchen and, after being mopped up, reappeared time and time again, despite the mains being turned off.

As they dealt with that, a tea dispenser started firing steaming tea at them as the door to the hall swung open and a pot plant was hurled up the stairs. As a crockery cupboard began to violently rattle. Phillip and his gran fled the house.



Whether an elaborate prank or paranormal phenomenon, whatever caused the burst of activity was then quiet for two years when, suddenly the lights in the house began cutting out, bed covers were thrown downstairs, pot plants overturned – spooky happenings that Jean put down to an entity she nicknamed “Mr Nobody.”

But when Diane was 15, and the family decided to decorate her room, the disturbances ramped up a notch.

Hearing a shout, the family rushed to the bedroom and found Diane cowering on the floor, dodging flying paint brushes and, as Jean watched a wallpaper roll began to unfurl and curl up into the air like a charmed snake. Then a heavy, mechanical carpet sweeper was lifted into the air and hurtled towards them as a curtain rail was ripped from the wall and thrown out of the window.

Joe, a Yorkshire miner, pulled his family out of the bedroom and slammed the door, shouting ‘that is enough’, but the crashing and banging continued in the empty room.

Terrified, Jean called in a local priest, Reverend Davies, who initially put the mishaps down to “subsidence”. But he later reported that a candlestick rose from the mantelpiece and hovered in front of his eyes and, in the next room, the contents of a crockery cupboard was found strewn across the floor – but not chipped or broken.



The clergyman had only one answer for the stricken family – “Move house.”

But the very same night, as Diane headed up to bed, the temperature suddenly dropped and, as the terrified girl turned round, the solid oak hall stand tipped over and pinned her to the stairs, with the whole family having to lift it from her.

As she climbed into bed, it’s reported, the bedclothes were ripped away, the mattress flew into the air and Diane was thrown on to the floor.

Over the next few weeks, objects flew around, a sandwich was found with enormous, inhuman teeth marks and the teenagers both suffered mysterious stomach pains.

When Joe’s deeply religious sister Maud came to stay, the poltergeist put on a display, lifting a jug of milk from the fridge before pouring it over her.



Shaken Maud then insisted on sharing a room with Jean but, as soon as the light turned off, four bulbs from the electric fire came loose and circled the room in a sinister light show. Maud’s gloves then lifted into the air and began beckoning her, As she launched into a chorus of Onward Christian Soldiers in a bid to exorcise evil, the suspended gloves mocked her by conducting her performance.

Maud left, saying “the devil is in that house.”



Another relative, a staunch Catholic, attempted an exorcism, spirinkling holy water in each room. But even as he said prayers, an egg appeared from nowhere and smashed, leaving the scent of flowers, and water began to stream down the walls.

A persistent drumming sound also started up, continuing all night, with the family failing to find its source.

That night, as Diane attempted to sleep, she was once more lifted into the air and dumped on the floor.

The following day, as Jean combed her hair, the family claimed a kitchen drawer slid open and flew across the room, hitting her in the back.

Then a brass crucifix, with a small figure of Jesus, flew off the kitchen mantelpiece and landed on Diane’s back, staying in place as she was a powerful magnet. Jean tried to pull the cross off her daughter, as the model of Jesus fell off, but the cross itself wouldn’t budge.



Finally, the crucifix dropped from a screaming Diane’s back and, when Jean lifted her daughter’s blouse, she saw a livid red cross – as if she’s been branded with hot metal – which was visible for three days.

On Easter Sunday, the family were horrified to discover every door in the house had been painted with a gold cross, upside down, perfectly executed as if with a stencil.

It was soon after that the family began to see the vision of a tall, dark figure, dressed in a dark monk’s robe, who first appeared to Joe and Jean in their bedroom.

Joe’s sister Rene, who was staying in the house, then felt a hand touch the back of her head while she was in bed and, when she opened her eyes, she saw the lower half of a man dressed in a black robe, who turned and walked out of the room.

A next door neighbour then reported turning around in her kitchen to see a tall, dark figure dressed in a black robe like a monk’s habit.



A few days later, Diane left the family in the living room and went to make coffee, but then let out a blood-curdling scream.

Jean and Philip rushed out to find Diane being dragged, seemingly by her cardigan, and they desperately tried to pull her down in a horrific tug of war.

After minutes of this deathly battle, it occurred to Phillip that, if Mr Nobody could physically touch his sister, then he could also be physically touched, and he reached out to try and pull the invisible arms off Diane, at which point its grip loosened and the three tumbled down the stairs.



It was only then they noticed a ring of red finger marks around Diane’s throat – suggesting the poltergeist had been trying to strangle her.

Evelyn Hollow tells the podcast that poltergeist activity is rarely reported as direct violence, in this way.

“The family are either in danger from an unseen supernatural force or they’re in danger from another person in the house, perhaps one of their own family members or neighbours, or they’re in danger from themselves.

“Regardless of what you believe this case is caused by, we’ve escalated to the point now of threat to life. And so it doesn’t matter if it’s supernatural or not, these people are in absolute danger.”

As a sceptic, psychologist Dr Ciaran O’Keefe adds that, in his opinion, there is no such thing as ghosts which can do physical harm, although he admits that many of these incidents, if true, are impossible to explain.



“I think we’ve got to face the reality of the situation and that is that, even from a team sceptic perspective,people are getting hurt,” he says. “So regardless of how we think about it, it’s incredibly terrifying for the family.

“If I was an investigator in this particular case, I would be coming in and I would be saying, genuinely, like Reverend Davey said, ‘let’s get out of here.’”

The infamous case inspired the 2012 horror movie, When the Lights Went Out, and Most Haunted presenter Yvette Fielding named it as the most scary venue she visited for the show.

Yvette told Metro.co.uk: “The most scary was a council house in Pontefract where nobody has been able to live for so long because of all the awful things that were happening there, and it’s such a normal place but so much poltergeist activity is happening there.”

Jean Pritchard lived in the house until 2001 but it has been empty since, with lovers of the paranormal often renting it for ‘investigations’.



“There have been investigations of the property and people have reported activity,” says Kieran. “They reported objects being thrown, objects moving since, a presence but also people actually being interacted with.”

He pointed out that reports of scratches and bruises caused by the Monk since are open to scrutiny.

“Psychologically, are we seeing something psychosomatic or people wanting that fame because they’re having the same phenomena happen to them that happened to the Pritchards?” he says.

“For me, the original case is the most interesting part and all the subsequent phenomena that we get post 2001, I feel there’s a little bit of storytelling going on there.”

The house has also become a popular destination for paranormal investigators.



In 2016 Steve Archibald, and his wife Carriefrom Pitch Black Investigations persuaded a group of intrepid paranormal enthusiasts to spend the night.

And Steve’s footage appears to show a pushchair be thrown by an invisible force down the same set of stairs where 14-year-old Diane Pritchard said to have been dragged by the hair by the monk.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And paranormal investigator Claire Cowell captured an image she believes shows the arm of the monk’s robe clutching rosary beads – also on the stairs.

Uncanny Cold Cases, episodes 1 and 2, are now available on BBC Sounds and all major podcast providers

News.title: PM is swiftly running out of lives – Olly Robbins blew his Mandelson story apart with series of truth grenades
News.content:
WE have just witnessed one of the most brutal demolition jobs in modern political history.

It may have been couched in Whitehall jargon. It may have been done with unflappable politeness and charm.





But over the course of two hours, Sir Olly Robbins successfully steamrollered Sir Keir Starmer’s version of events surrounding the appointment of Peter Mandelson.

This is the man who just yesterday was accused by the PM of orchestrating a “deliberate” cover-up over the ex-US ambassador’s failed vetting.

We were told Starmer sacked the Foreign Office chief for the “unforgivable” crime of unilaterally overruling the advice of the security services to hand Mandelson his clearance.

In short, the PM tried to pin the entire fiasco on Robbins and hoped he would, like so many others, go quietly into the night.

It now seems a catastrophic miscalculation.

Robbins came armed with the receipts and methodically detonated them like grenades under Starmer’s story.

Downing Street took a “dismissive approach” to Mandelson’s vetting, he said, while the Cabinet Office originally did not think that any vetting “at all” was required.

Starmer’s private office applied “pressure” on him to fast-track the appointment in time for Trump’s inauguration.



By the time Robbins had started in his own job, Mandelson was already receiving highly-classified documents despite lacking clearance.

Far from being a conniving mandarin, most people watching his cool performance will come away with the impression of a diligent official simply doing his master’s bidding.

And then other bombs started to drop…

Robbins told us that No10 had tried to appoint Starmer’s then comms chief Matthew Doyle into a top diplomatic posting.

The axed Foreign Office chief claimed he was even told to keep this bizarre process secret from the then Foreign Secretary David Lammy.



Doyle, of course, would later be made a peer before having to resign the Labour whip over his own relationship with a convicted paedophile.

That Starmer tried to parachute another controversial pal into a plum job opens up a whole new world of pain he really doesn’t need right now.

Which makes it staggering that No10 could be so politically dense as to make an enemy on Robbins knowing he possessed such damaging ammunition.

The question now is how Starmer responds.

If Starmer tries to deny Robbins’ claims, he better make sure his challenge is more than water-tight.



Robbins certainly spoke like a man who knew what he was talking about.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Labour MPs seem in no mood to launch a leadership challenge right now, especially before a set of tough May local elections.

But today’s evidence felt seismic in its gravity, and potentially pivotal in the life chances of a Prime Minister running out of lives.

News.title: Horror as mom & six kids aged 3-11 killed when entire house explodes leaving them trapped behind wall of flames
News.content:
TRAPPED IN TERROR Horror as mom & six kids aged 3-11 killed when entire house explodes leaving them trapped behind wall of flames

A MOM and her six young children were killed in a horror house explosion that left them trapped behind a raging wall of flames.

The blast ripped through the family home in Pennsylvania, shaking nearby houses and sending firefighters racing to the scene.



But by the time crews arrived at the address in Lamar Township, near Mill Hall, it was already too late.



Seven people – all from the same family -were trapped inside the burning building on Sunday morning.

Rescuers were unable to enter as the home was completely engulfed in flames, police said.

All seven tragically died at the scene.

Authorities named the victims as Sarah Stoltzfus, 34, and her six children – four boys aged 11, 10, five and three, and two girls aged eight and six.



The family were members of the Old Order Amish Church community.

Footage showed members of the Amish community gathering at the scene later, helping to clear the wreckage and pay their respects after the devastating loss.

Sarah Stoltzfus is survived by her husband, David Stoltzfus.

The cause of the blast is under investigation, but police say a propane leak inside the home may have triggered the explosion.



Exterior propane tanks did not explode and were not contributing factors.

Horrified neighbour Christina Duck described the terrifying moment the blast hit.

She said: “And I heard a boom and I could feel it and I got up and looked out the window and I could see the flames through the windows and I come running outside and within a minute the whole house was completely engulfed.”

The neighbour added the family had only moved in a couple of months ago and the children were often seen playing outside.

By the time firefighters reached the home, there was no chance of a rescue.



“There was no saving that house, it went up so fast,” she said.

News.title: Boy, 12, to stand trial accused of sexually assaulting woman in her 60s who was left in serious condition in hospital
News.content:
'SEX ATTACK' Boy, 12, to stand trial accused of sexually assaulting woman in her 60s who was left in serious condition in hospital

A TWELVE-year-old boy is set to stand trial charged with sexually assaulting a woman who was left in a serious condition in hospital.

The defendant, who can’t be named, was charged last month after the woman was discovered at an address in Birmingham.



He appeared at Birmingham Crown Court today accused of wounding and sexual assault.



The boy, who is separately charged with intentional strangulation, was not required to speak during the hearing.

No pleas were entered but a provisional trial date was set for October this year.

Judge Simon Drew KC remanded the boy into secure accommodation ahead of a further hearing at the same court in August.

He said: “The next hearing that I can definitely say will take place will be on the 13th of August and the case will be listed for trial on October 5th.”



The alleged sex attack took place on March 18 this year at the woman’s home.

Police said she was taken to hospital in a serious condition but there is no update on her condition.

The intentional strangulation charge allegedly relates to another incident where a woman was confronted in the street.

A West Midlands Police spokesperson said: “Our enquiries remain ongoing, but we understand how concerning this will be within the community.



“Our officers will be continuing to provide reassurance in the local area.

“If anyone has any information regarding suspicious behaviour on March 18 or in the days leading up to last Wednesday, details can be submitted via the Major Incident Public Portal or via 101, quoting log 4888 of March 18.”

News.title: Girl, 12, dies after getting hair stuck in pool suction pump leaving her trapped underwater while swimming with pals
News.content:
TRAGIC END Girl, 12, dies after getting hair stuck in pool suction pump leaving her trapped underwater while swimming with pals

A 12-YEAR-OLD girl has died after her hair got stuck in a pool’s suction system, trapping her underwater.

Laura Pereira Camargo was swimming with friends in their pool in Mirassol, Brazil when she suddenly became trapped.





She was stuck underwater for a full five minutes, reports said.

When she was pulled from the pool, the young girl was in a critical condition.

Emergency services arrived at the scene and Laura was rushed to a local clinic.



She was then transferred to a specialist children’s hospital in Sao Jose do Rio Preto.

Doctors fought to save her but nothing could be done.

The horrific accident took place on April 17.

Laura died two days later after suffering multiple organ failure and complications, including bacterial pneumonia.



The tragedy shocked the local community, with relatives and friends paying tribute to the young girl.

She was described as much-loved by those who knew her.

Her funeral was scheduled to take place today.

It comes after a 12-year-old boy was left brain dead after being sucked into a hot tub while on holiday in Italy.

The incident occurred in the spa at Duca di Montefeltro Hotel in Pennabilli, near Rimini.



Matteo Brandimarti was holidaying in the Italian town with his family when tragedy struck on Easter Sunday.

At around 10am in the morning the family decided to use the hotel’s facilities to relax.

But Matteo became trapped in the hot tub after his leg was sucked into the nozzle while the hydromassage function was still on.

The boy was dragged under the water where he was stuck for almost five minutes.

Hotel staff managed to cut the main power supply which turned off the pump, but Matteo was already in critical condition.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Matteo was rushed to hospital and placed on life support equipment, but on April 9 he was pronounced brain dead.

His life support was then turned off, local media said.

News.title: Pals joked my fiance could be a murderer after whirlwind love, his chilling confession led to a cold case investigation
News.content:
WHEN Dr Caroline Muirhead met a rugged farmer on Tinder she thought she’d finally found her dream man.

But shortly after their whirlwind engagement, Alexander “Sandy” McKellar made a chilling confession that would change everything.





He told her he had killed a man and buried his body, with the help of his twin brother Robert, on a remote Scottish estate.

“He’s said, ‘he’s on the estate. You jog past him every day. He’s right beneath your feet when you shoot your clay pigeons’,” Caroline says.

That man was cyclist Tony Parsons, 63 – a cancer survivor from Clackmannanshire in Scotland who had mysteriously vanished after setting out on a 100-mile charity bike ride across the country in September 2017.



In an extraordinary twist, it would be Caroline herself who ultimately led police to his body – after secretly marking the remote burial site in the Scottish Highlands with a crushed Red Bull can.

Her evidence proved crucial in finally solving the case, helping detectives recover Tony’s remains in January 2021.

The shocking story – and the devastating toll it took – is now told by Caroline in the three-part Netflix documentary Should I Marry A Murderer?.

In 2020, Caroline, then 29, was rebuilding her life after a difficult breakup.



Working as a pathologist in Glasgow, she dealt with death daily – but hoped for something brighter in her personal life.

She joined Tinder and was instantly drawn to Sandy – a towering gamekeeper living in isolation on the sprawling Auch Estate in the Scottish Highlands.

His profile read: “6ft 4 Highlander: Lonely contractor looking for someone to keep him warm on cold nights on the farm”.

Attracted to his rugged lifestyle, Caroline struck up a conversation – and he quickly invited her to visit his remote home, around 90 minutes outside Glasgow.



Before she left, a friend unwittingly joked: “What if he turns out to be a murderer?”

The relationship moved fast.

“After our first date things moved quite fast. Because he was so far away you’d have to go for the weekend,” she says.

“I was falling for him, hook, line and sinker,” she says.

She soon became immersed in his world – spending weekends on the estate and growing close to his twin brother Robert, with whom he had grown up and worked.



“I loved him and I felt loved,” she says.

They even bonded over an unusual shared connection – death.

“We both had to deal with death on a daily basis,” she says.

“Postmortems were a large part of my job,” she says.

Sandy, who culled deer on the estate and ran a hunting agency, was comfortable around it too.



“He was very very equipped with knife skills and handling meat,” she says.

But cracks soon began to show.

The brothers drank heavily and took drugs, and Caroline, who also took drugs with them, noticed unsettling changes in Sandy’s personality.

On one occasion, Robert warned her: “My brother’s not right in the head. He’s not well,” she says.



“I was blind-sided to the red flags,” she admits.

Within months, the relationship escalated into talk of marriage – and she announced their engagement, leaving friends and family stunned.

Sandy told her: “I’ve never loved and trusted someone as much as I love and trust you.”

In November 2020, Sandy made a confession that would unravel everything though.

“He said something happened in September 2017,” Caroline says.



He described how he and Robert had been drinking after a hunting trip before driving back to the estate – over the legal limit.

“He said a big truck came with full beam and blinded him,” she says.

“In that moment he then hit a cyclist,” she says.

That cyclist was Tony Parsons.

“He said, ‘he was hit at high speed. There’s no way he was alive,’” she says.



Caroline immediately questioned him.

“I said, ‘Did you call for help?’” she says.

“He said, ‘What would we have done? If we’d called the police I’d have lost everything.

“We’d have gone to jail and lost our lives for a man that should never have been there’,” she says.



He insisted it had been an accident.

Despite her horror, Caroline says: “I believed what he was saying.

“I was so stunned I told him that I loved him, because he was crying, and that good people make mistakes,” she says.

But everything changed later that night.

She searched online and found missing person appeals for Tony Parsons, a grandfather and former navy veteran who had vanished without a trace.



The reality of what she had been told began to sink in.

Then came a second, even more disturbing request.

Sandy told her the burial site was about to be disturbed and asked for her help moving the body.

“If we can get rid of this problem then we can have a life together,” she claims he told her.



“He was asking me how long it takes to burn a human body and I was like, ‘it depends on the state of decomposition,’” she says.

“And he said ‘I poured a s*** tonne of bleach on that man, Caroline’,” she says.

That was the moment she knew she had to go to police.

She reported everything in late December 2020.



But detectives needed one crucial piece of evidence – the body.

So Caroline made a decision.

“I said, ‘Sandy, if you want me to help you with this you need to show me exactly where you buried him’,” she says.

Trusting her, he took her to the spot.

“He taps the ground and says ‘here’,” she says.



With nothing to mark the remote location, Caroline secretly crushed a Red Bull can into the ground.

It would later prove vital.

Trying to maintain normality, she continued seeing Sandy while secretly helping police.

“I was trying to almost stage normality because we were beyond not coping,” she says.



She later sent officers his live location and armed police arrested both brothers in December 2020.

“I hated myself. I felt like a rat. I felt like a liar,” she says.

But without a body, the case stalled. The brothers were released on bail just two days later.

Caroline was left terrified they would realise she had exposed them.

She moved back in with her parents, living in fear.



But in a confusing and emotionally fraught period, she drifted back towards Sandy.

Then came a chilling new revelation.

Robert pulled her aside and told her the truth about what had really happened.

“He said ‘Caroline, I don’t know what Sandy’s told you but you have to understand when we hit that man it happened very fast. He flew over the car. We got out and when we walked towards him, he was alive’,” she says.



“I thought he’d been killed on impact. I was like, f***,” she says.

Robert went on to explain they had left Tony at the roadside.

“He said he moved him to the side of the road with the bike for them to be able to change vehicles and come back,” she says.

“And I was like, ‘Robert, you left him alone?’” she says.

They later returned, placed him in a tarpaulin, and took him back to the estate.



He was kept overnight before being buried.

“That same vehicle was used by the hunting clients the next day. Then they buried Tony Parsons once the clients left,” she says.

“In my head this wasn’t then a hit and run. This was potentially murder,” she says.

When she confronted Sandy, secretly recording him, he told her: “It was either his life or my life.”



In January 2021, forensic teams began digging at the site Caroline had marked.

Professor Dame Lorna Dawson was among those present.

“We were digging down to about 30–35cm,” she says.

“There’s red material here… it looked like the clothing Mr Parsons was wearing.



“You could see the fingerless gloves..

“And indeed, there was a ring on his wedding finger.”

As Tony’s body was recovered, she recalls: “He was lifted onto the stretcher and as he was carried out the sun came out between the clouds.

“We all stood with our heads bowed and we all said a little silent prayer,” she says.



The discovery triggered panic.

A worker mentioned the Red Bull can – and Sandy immediately realised it was Caroline who had told Police what had happened.

“You f***ing little bitch you f***ing did this,” he shouted over the phone.

He later turned up at her home.



“I honestly thought he was going to kill me,” she says.

Yet emotionally, she remained conflicted.

“We had a bond which was obviously not healthy at all but there was a bond and there was an awful lot of love,” she says.

But the truth was undeniable.

A post-mortem confirmed Tony had suffered catastrophic injuries — but had been alive after the collision.



In another recorded conversation in which he discussed Tony, Sandy told Caroline: “F*** stupid c*** shouldn’t have f***ing been there.”

In December 2021, the twins were rearrested.

They attempted to plead guilty to causing death by dangerous driving but were instead charged with murder.

As the trial approached, Caroline – broken by what had happened and feeling unsupported by Police – collapsed under the pressure.



“I was so ashamed of who I was and what I’d become,” she says.

She failed to appear in court on the first day as a key witness.

When proceedings resumed, the Crown accepted a reduced plea of culpable homicide.

The court heard Tony had been struck on the A82 between Bridge of Orchy and Tyndrum.

Though badly injured, he had still been alive – and no help was called.



He died within 30 minutes.

In 2023, justice was finally delivered.

Alexander “Sandy” McKellar, 31, was jailed for 12 years.

Robert, also 31, received five years and three months.



Looking back, Caroline is clear.

“He did take an innocent man’s life. So for me he is a coward and a killer,” she says.

Now rebuilding her life by the coast, she is receiving psychiatric support and trying to move forward.

“I am so lucky to be able to move forward with my life,” she says.



She has also found love again.

“I met someone new who is incredibly kind. When you love yourself you will attract healthy love,” she says.

For Tony’s family, however, the pain remains.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His widow Margaret has previously said: “When they get out of jail… I am… left with a life sentence.” The family don’t appear in the documentary.

Should I Marry A Murderer? launches April 29 on Netflix

News.title: 'Someone tried breaking into my home and I couldn’t believe who it was'
News.content:
'Someone tried breaking into my home and I couldn’t believe who it was'

One man documented the moment he caught someone in the act trying to break into his flat after days of odd behaviour, and he couldn't believe who the suspect was

View Image The man couldn't believe who'd been trying to get inside his home (stock image)

A man has shared the thrilling moment when he caught someone in the middle of a suspected 'break in' attempt, and was left baffled to learn who it was.

‌



One fear that most people have, whether they rent or own their homes, is that someone will break in to their home without their permission or knowledge. This fear came true for one man named Tommy, Mellor, who took to social media to share the moment he stopped a 'break in' attempt in action after a few days of off behaviour, but the suspect wasn't who he'd expected it to be.

‌



Taking to TikTok, Tommy explained that he knew someone had been near his apartment, as he would often find his door mat, which he has laying inside the entrance of his home, being on the other side of his front door.

‌



"Someone has been trying to break into my apartment," Tommy said at the start of his video, which showed some shadows moving around on the other side of his front door.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

He went on to explain to viewers that over the past few days when he come home from work, the mat that he keeps at the entrance of his home has mysteriously been laying out in the hallway, on the other side of the door, which he showed proof of in the video.

‌



"And today, I finally figured out who it was," Tommy revealed. "I finally caught them in the act."

The video then cut to Tommy zooming in on his door mat, which was moving side to side, before a white paw appeared from the other side of the door, dragging the mat towards them under the door.

Tommy then opened the door to reveal a grey and white cat looking up at Tommy, unsure of what to do next as he'd been caught in the act.

‌



Several people soon took to the comments to share their thoughts on the unexpected outcome, as some went on to defend the kleptomaniac cat for his actions.

"I'm this cats lawyer and you only have circumstantial evidence," one viewer jokingly commented. Meanwhile, someone else also said: "Do you have proof the mat is yours? Kitty makes a compelling ownership argument."

A third viewer shared: "My cat pulls the bathroom mat out from under the door all the time. I just thank her for redecorating."

‌



"Ok but HOW did the cat know the mat was there??" someone else wondered.

Several people also questioned the possibility of the crime, as they wondered why there were such a big gap between the floor and the front door.

"Am I the only one questioning why there is such a gap underneath the door," one person said. Another wrote: "My question would be. WHY THE F. is there so much space under the door."

Article continues below

A third also questioned: "Sorry I have questions. Is someone letting their cat free roam in an apartment building??"

News.title: DEFRA warning to easyJet, Ryanair, Jet2 passengers over duty free ban
News.content:
DEFRA warning to easyJet, Ryanair, Jet2 passengers over duty free ban

A new response highlighted how passengers can fall foul of £5,000 fines - and having their lunch seized and destroyed

View Image People arriving UK Border and passport control could get £5,000 fines for bringing banned food - even bought at duty free (Image: Getty)

The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) has given an update for anyone thinking of bringing food into the UK on their flight. Officials have restated rules to stop an outbreak of devastating foot and mouth disease in the UK after a number of cases found in Europe - the latest being in Greece and Cyprus last month.

‌



As it stands any passengers using airlines such as TUI, Ryanair, Wizz, easyJet and Jet2 will have their bags checked - and have certain food seized and destroyed - including some bought at duty free on the trip. Travellers are not able to bring cattle, sheep, goat, and pig meat, as well as dairy products, from EU countries into Great Britain for personal use.

‌



DEFRA said: “This includes bringing items like sandwiches, cheese, cured meats, raw meats or milk into Great Britain – regardless of whether it is packed or packaged or whether it has been bought at duty free.” A new outbreak has been found in Cyprus aand Tory

‌



Dr Neil Hudson asked Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, Emma Reynolds in a new parliamentary written question if any extra measures are in place: “In light of the Foot and Mouth Outbreak in Cyprus, what additional biosecurity measures are in place for people travelling to the UK from Cyprus?”

In reply Dame Angela Eagle Minister of State in the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs said: “Defra banned personal imports of pig and ruminant meat and dairy products from the EU into England in April 2025. The ban remains in place. Equivalent measures are in place in Wales and Scotland.”

Ten airlines add extra charges as jet fuel crisis gets worse READ MORE :

In a recent Facebook post DEFRA added: “Think you know what foods you can bring back into Great Britain from the EU? Our personal import rules are there to protect animals and the environment from serious disease outbreaks such as foot and mouth disease and African swine fever. Viruses like these can survive in food products for weeks or even months and have devastating effects on rural businesses if they infect animals.

‌



"To protect our animals from the devastating effects of diseases like foot and mouth, it’s illegal to bring meats such as lamb, pork or beef or dairy products from the EU into GB in your luggage. This means items such as cheese, cured or raw meats, sandwiches and milk, including duty free purchases.””

It is now illegal for travellers from all EU countries entering Great Britain to bring items like sandwiches, cheese, cured meats, raw meats or milk into the country. DEFRA added: “This is regardless of whether it is packed or packaged or whether it has been bought at duty free.

“Those found with these items will need to either surrender them at the border or will have them seized and destroyed. In serious cases, those found with these items run the risk of incurring fines of up to £5,000 in England.“

‌



In a release last month DEFRA UK Chief Veterinary Officer Dr Christine Middlemiss said: “A case of Foot and Mouth disease has been confirmed in Greece, we are in contact with our European counterparts to understand the latest situation.

“Robust plans are already in place to minimise the risk of disease incursion to support Britain’s farming community and food security.

“Livestock keepers are urged to continue exercising the upmost vigilance for signs of disease, follow scrupulous biosecurity and report any suspicion of disease immediately to the Animal and Plant Health Agency.”

News.title: Sarah Ferguson has 'no plans to leave' bolthole as cousin reveals why she’s hiding
News.content:
Sarah Ferguson has 'no plans to leave' bolthole as cousin reveals why she’s hiding

Despite it being revealed that Sarah Ferguson has been hiding away at a ski resort in Austria - sources say she has no plans to leave the Alpine retreat

View 3 Images Fergie has been pictured in Austria (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Sarah Ferguson has no plans to leave her Austrian ski chalet despite her hiding place being rumbled, according to a source. After not being seen in public for almost seven months after becoming embroiled in th Epstein scandal, she has eventually been tracked down to a reported £2,000-a-night ski chalet in Austria as she attempted to move around the alpine village incognito.

‌



Mystery had surrounded her whereabouts ever since she was repeatedly named in a tranche of documents released by US investigators probing the late billionaire sex offender's crimes, with calls for her to give evidence in the US on what she knew. But despite her location now being revealed and calls growing for her to speak to authorities, a source says she has now plans to leave her Austrian bolthole.

‌



View 3 Images It has been revealed where Sarah Ferguson has been hiding out (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

‌



They told The Sun: “She has no immediate plans to leave. Even though her location has finally been revealed. The resort has got everything you’d want for a lengthy stay.” It comes after a relative of Fergie’s, her cousin-by-marriage Martin Barrantes spoke out, saying he had spoken to the former Duchess of York in recent months and explained her reason for hiding out.

He told the Daily Mail: "I have spoken to her [and] can tell you that she just wants to protect her children and her grandchildren.” Barrantes — who is the nephew of Fergies late stepfather, the Argentinian polo player Hector Barrantes - added: “Sarah is going through a difficult moment, and I wanted to send her our support; she is a valued member of our family. Sarah was perhaps foolish to trust him and take such confidence from him, and I am sure she regrets that now.”

It comes as the Mirror previously revealed that Fergie has not been contacted by any member of the Royal Family since she was unceremoniously stripped of the title she traded off for decades, despite being divorced from Andrew for 30 years. One friend said: "Sarah is living in fear right now. She's not immune to everything that is happening. She realises how serious everything is, and she is not coping with it.

‌



View 3 Images Fergie with ex-husband Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

“She is definitely worried about returning home to the UK and is relying on the kindness of friends to help her through the situation. But she knows she can't keep moving around forever. Sarah feels she has been abandoned by the royal family and has been treated very unfairly. She is at a complete loss over what to do.

Rumours in the publishing world have continued to gather pace that Fergie is also hoping to relaunch her shattered literary career with a tell all memoir, but she has demanded a fee of more than £1million. A source said: "One thing is for certain, she is desperately short of cash."

‌



The Epstein scandal hit Fergie last September when it emerged despite publicly disowning him - prompting a string of charities to drop her as a patron.

Meanwhile, in documents released in January, Fergie appeared to say to Epstein in an email: “I am at your service. Just marry me.” In another email to Epstein, she made a crude comment about her daughter Eugenie's love life and described him as the "brother I have always wished for" and even called the criminal a "legend".

Article continues below

Another appears to show her begging the paedophile for a job as his house assistant, and it also emerged she appeared to take her daughters Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie to visit him in Florida just days after he was released from prison in 2008.

It led to a US lawmaker writing to the former duchess, urging her to testify to Congress about Epstein. Congressman Suhas Subramanyam requested that she give evidence in a government investigation into Epstein’s sex trafficking operations. As a non-US citizen, Ferguson, 66, is not compelled to appear before Congress or respond to the request.

News.title: Popular airline reduces Europe flights and cancels others until June 14
News.content:
Popular airline reduces Europe flights and cancels others until June 14

It comes after reports that Europe potentially has about six weeks' worth of jet fuel left

View 3 Images The airline updated its Middle East statement situation (stock image) (Image: Getty)

A popular airline has changed some of its flight plans for next month. This affects a few flights in Europe that are not making enough money to keep flying because kerosene prices are rising. However, the airline emphasises that there is no shortage of kerosene.

‌



KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, which connects to 19 UK airports, recently issued an update to its flight schedule for the coming month, noting several adjustments. On its website, KLM said: "This concerns a limited number of flights within Europe that, due to rising kerosene costs, are currently no longer financially viable to operate.

‌



"There is no kerosene shortage. KLM will operate 80 fewer return flights to and from Schiphol, which is less than 1% of its European flights during that period."

‌



It added: "Passengers affected by these changes will be rebooked onto the next available flight. As these are destinations KLM serves multiple times a day — such as London and Düsseldorf — travellers can usually be accommodated quickly. KLM expects a busy May holiday period and is making sure passengers can travel to their holiday destinations as planned."

In mid-April 2026, the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that Europe has about six weeks' worth of jet fuel left, which could lead to shortages and flight cancellations by early June. The crisis is caused by conflicts in the Middle East that are blocking the Strait of Hormuz, preventing vital supplies from passing through. This situation creates serious risks for summer travel, and airlines are keeping a close eye on their fuel stocks.

View 3 Images KLM will operate 80 fewer return flights to and from Schiphol

‌



Derren Nathan, head of equity research at Hargreaves Lansdown, said: "Brent Crude prices have climbed five per cent to over $95 per barrel just days after they fell by about $12 to $85 on Friday on hopes of the resumption of energy cargoes through the Strait of Hormuz.

"Further downstream, the crisis is starting to have tangible effects, with several airlines cutting back on less profitable routes and the International Energy Agency warning that European jet fuel supplies could run out by early June. Interest rate expectations continue to bounce around, hanging on every twist and turn in the Gulf."

KLM has also decided to cancel flights to and from Dubai until June 14. The airline said: "Despite recent reporting about the situation in the Middle East, the current circumstances in the region still bring uncertainties. To provide clarity and certainty to travellers scheduled to fly to Dubai in the coming weeks, the cancellations have been extended by one month."

‌



View 3 Images KLM stressed "there is no kerosene shortage"

In an update shared today (April 21), KLM says it has decided to cancel flights to and from Riyadh and Dammam up to and including June 14. It added: "To provide clarity and certainty to travellers scheduled to fly to Riyadh and Dammam in the coming weeks, the cancellations have been extended."

KLM said: "The safety of our passengers and crew is always our top priority. We understand that this decision has a significant impact on our travellers and are doing everything possible to keep them well informed. Passengers whose flights have been cancelled will be notified personally.

Article continues below

"They can change their flight or request a refund on the KLM website. We continue to closely monitor the situation and remain in contact with the relevant authorities."

News.title: New Lloyds announcement to 'change the way' homes are bought and sold
News.content:
New Lloyds announcement to 'change the way' homes are bought and sold

It has created a new partnership aimed at making the process less stressful

View 3 Images Lloyds’ partnership aims to help limit the number of home transactions falling through (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA)

A partnership to help take the headache out of the home-buying process has been launched by mortgage giant Lloyds Banking Group, estate agency Connells Group and conveyancing provider LMS (Legal Marketing Services). Those behind the announcement said it will reshape the way homes are bought and sold across England and Wales, with customers benefiting from a simpler process.

‌



The digital home buyer service has been developed to cut “points of frustration” such as duplicated checks and long waiting times. Customers should experience a smoother journey with fewer questions and less chasing, according to those behind the initiative.

‌



The service aims to tackle issues with checks taking place earlier and information shared digitally between relevant parties using LMS’s property transaction network, a shared data-exchange platform. It also aims to tackle the issue of repetitive requests for identity verification and minimise “late surprises” about properties.

‌



View 3 Images Buying and selling homes is notoriously difficult (Image: d3sign via Getty Images)

The service runs on residential sale and purchase transactions within England and Wales, involving Connells branches, LMS‑panel conveyancers, and Lloyds Banking Group as the lender.

Housing Secretary Steve Reed said: “Too many people who have bought or sold a home will know this feeling all too well – months of waiting, chasing and worrying, with sales liable to fall through at any moment. It can quickly become a living nightmare. It doesn’t need to be this difficult and that is why we have set out bold proposals to shake up the home-buying and selling process.

‌



“I’m pleased to see Lloyds Banking Group, Connells Group and LMS showing what’s possible by getting the right information to the right people earlier, cutting the delays and uncertainty that make moving home so stressful.”

View 3 Images There are hopes it could change things (Image: Bloomberg, Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Andrew Asaam, homes director, Lloyds Banking Group, said: “The process of buying or selling your home is too stressful, too slow, too laborious and often collapses through no fault of your own.

Article continues below

"With this new digital service, we aim to cut the stress, increase the speed, reduce the workload for customers and limit the number of transactions that fall through. This could change the way we buy and sell homes.”

Chris Rosindale, chief operating officer at Connells Group, which has more than 1,200 branches, said: “We believe in reform that makes the system faster, more transparent and more reliable and are excited to be part of transformation in the sector.”

Nick Chadbourne, chief executive at LMS, said: “This initiative signals a serious move away from siloed processes and toward genuine market-wide reform.”

News.title: Tiny button on your car mirror actually has a purpose that few drivers know about
News.content:
Tiny button on your car mirror actually has a purpose that few drivers know about

A woman has taken to TikTok to reveal that the small button located on car rear view mirrors actually has a function - and it's come as a surprise to a lot of people

View 3 Images A little known car mirror hack could make driving safer and more comfortable (Image: Getty Images)

Drivers have been surprised to discover a hidden feature on the rear view mirrors in their cars - and it could save lives. A viral TikTok video has shed light on the little-known function, and it seems there's always something new to learn about our vehicles.

‌



The clip, posted by user @chequanxiaoqiao, highlighted the purpose of a small, often-overlooked button on car mirrors. In the video, she explains: "The lights of the rear car are too dazzling when driving at night.

‌



"We just need to press this little wrench under the rear view mirror-you can turn on the anti-glare function." This little adjustment is designed to reduce glare from the headlights of vehicles behind you - by flipping the lever or pressing the button, you can dim the reflection and make night time driving safer.

‌



I'm a baggage handler and one type of suitcase is less likely to be thrown READ MORE :

View 3 Images The button on a rear view mirror has a useful purpose - but not many people know about it (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The video has racked up hundreds of thousands of views, sparking a flurry of comments. One viewer remarked: "Wait a minute. You mean to tell me there was an anti-glare function all the nights I nearly drove off the road."

Another added: "Why am I learning this now?" And a third wrote: "This is game changing, I am a cab driver and work all hours so will definitely try it out at night."

‌



It comes after an expert warned drivers to 'never do this' if they ever put the wrong type of fuel in their car.

Alicia Hempsted, car insurance expert at MoneySuperMarket, urged motorists not to start their car, if possible. If you've already started it, turn off the ignition straight away.

Alicia said: "Misfuelling is a potentially expensive mistake that can catch drivers out all year around, although recently there has been an increase in online searches for information about what to do if you accidentally put the wrong fuel in your car.

‌



View 3 Images An expert has advised what to do if you fill up with the wrong fuel (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

"If it happens to you, it's important to know how to respond, as misfuelling can seriously damage your car if not dealt with quickly. If possible, don't start your car. Starting your engine after putting in the wrong fuel can increase repair costs by hundreds or even thousands of pounds.

"If you've already started it, switch off the ignition as soon as possible. Move your car to a safe place by putting it into neutral and rolling the vehicle and call your breakdown provider or garage to drain and flush the tank."

Article continues below

She added: "Misfuelling is not typically covered by car insurance, so it isn't a mistake to take lightly. In most cases, you will need to add additional misfuelling insurance to your policy to include that protection, although some comprehensive policies may include misfuelling under accidental damage.

"Make sure you check your insurance cover to ensure you have the right protection in place should this happen to you."

News.title: Prince Harry marks 15 years since life-changing expedition with poignant statement
News.content:
Prince Harry marks 15 years since life-changing expedition with poignant statement

In 2011, the Duke of Sussex undertook a mammoth expedition to the North Pole to raise money for charity, with the days-long trek securing a world record

Prince Harry praises Walking With the Wounded group in video call

Prince Harry has marked 15 years since he undertook a life-changing expedition to raise money for charity, sharing a poignant statement about the mammoth undertaking.

‌



On April 16 2011, Armed Forces charity, Walking With The Wounded, joined by Expedition Patron, Prince Harry and a team of injured veterans, made history by reaching the geographical North Pole. The team completed the gruelling 200-mile challenge in 13 days and covered the greatest distance of any polar expedition that season.

‌



The expedition saw the team battling temperatures as low as minus 50 degrees Celsius and pulling their equipment in pulks. Their achievement secured a world-record as the first unsupported team of injured veterans to reach the North Pole.

‌



View 3 Images Prince Harry travelled to the North Pole in 2011 for charity (Image: Walking With the Wounded/Supplied)

The expedition raised vital funds for the WWTW charity while also thrusting the organisation into the spotlight. But most importantly, the trip proved that veterans, especially those injured during service, could still achieve incredible feats after they left the Armed Forces.

The team included WWTW Expedition Patron, Prince Harry, Expedition Leader and Polar Expert, Inge Solheim, WWTW Founder and CEO, Ed Parker, Simon Daglish and four wounded Servicemen, Captain Guy Disney, Sergeant Steve Young, Private Jaco Van Gass and Captain Martin Hewitt.

‌



In honour of the 15-year anniversary of the mammoth undertaking, the Duke of Sussex reunited with members of the original expedition team on a video call, reflecting on the challenge and the lasting impact it has had on those involved.

View 3 Images The expedition raised vital funds for the Walking With the Wounded charity (Image: Walking With the Wounded/Supplied)

Speaking candidly about the expedition, Harry told the charity organisation: "I was honoured to join Walking With The Wounded as Expedition Patron to the North Pole in 2011. The veteran march across the ice served as a powerful reminder of the tenacity and courage of those who serve and who’ve been injured in the line of duty."

‌



“Fifteen years on, I remain immensely proud of what these guys accomplished with WWTW. This incredible expedition helped change public perception at such a crucial time. It shone a light on the importance of supporting those who served, and it encouraged thousands more veterans to speak up and come forward.

"It's always a privilege to stand alongside the veteran community and to support the vital work of Walking With The Wounded.”

View 3 Images Harry reunited with the expedition team to mark 15 years since the trek (Image: Walking With the Wounded/Supplied)

‌



Alongside confronting the natural obstacles and harsh environment, each member of the expedition team sustained serious injuries while serving the United Kingdom on operations overseas. Fifteen years later, WWTW continues to support veterans and their families across the UK, providing employment support, mental health care and tailored support care coordination to empower those who have served.

Prince Harry is said to maintain a close relationship with the men he trekked to the North Pole with, with one member of his team recently publicly backing the Duke’s decision to continue to fight for paid security in the UK. Eton-educated Alex Rayner told the Daily Mail last month that Harry serving two tours of duty in Afghanistan when he was in the Army make him more vulnerable to UK security threats, adding that he thinks Harry’s taxpayer funded police protection while in his home country should be reinstated.

Article continues below

He said: "To ask him to pay for it privately feels a tiny bit spiteful, given that there are other members of the Royal Family who receive it who do far less. This guy was flying Apaches in a conflict and we’ve got the Invictus Games coming up in Birmingham. Are we not supporting him for that?"

News.title: Sister of murdered MP Jo Cox warns another politician 'will be killed' amid far-right surge
News.content:
Sister of murdered MP Jo Cox warns another politician 'will be killed' amid far-right surge

Labour MP Kim Leadbeater issued the stark warning as she said she never thought she would see the rise of 'racism, homophobia, misogyny' and 'sexism' we are seeing in the UK today

View 5 Images MP Kim Leadbeater talks to British Vogue about the rise of the far right ahead of the tenth anniversary of her sister's murder

The sister of murdered MP Jo Cox has warned that another politician “could and possibly will be killed” as the country suffers a surge in far right hate.

‌



Labour MP Kim Leadbeater opened up ahead of June's ten year anniversary of her sister’s murder. She told how she never thought in her lifetime she would see the rise of ‘racism, homophobia, misogyny’ and ‘sexism’ we are seeing in the UK today, and issued a stark warning about the very real threat of violence.

‌



Her sister, Jo, was murdered in broad daylight in 2016 by one of her own constituents. Her killer was a neo-Nazi who shouted “Put Britain first” as he shot and stabbed her.

‌



View 5 Images Kim Leadbeater with sister Jo Cox who was murdered by a neo-Nazi

Arrogant driver who killed young woman smirks outside court before crying at being jailed READ MORE :

During an interview with British Vogue, she was asked if instead of 'gentler politics', as had been the hope, things had got worse since her sister's death and were currently 'dangerously tense'. She said: "I totally agree.

“That’s why this 10-year anniversary is so important to me: for us to have those conversations. The toxicity in 2016 around the Brexit referendum, the division that we saw in communities, was dreadful. Obviously, my family, more than any, paid the ultimate price for that.”

‌



Speaking of Reform UK's growth and the extremist views that are becoming more openly discussed in the UK, Kim said: “(The government) left that space free to be filled with negativity, doom and gloom, how bad everything is. You can have polarisation in politics and you can have dreadful things being said and done.

View 5 Images MP Kim Leadbeater talks about her 'ridiculous' job as a politician (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

‌



“I totally agree that racism, homophobia, misogyny, sexism… we’re seeing it coming back in a way that I never thought I’d see again in my lifetime. You can also have a brilliant country full of amazing people. Those two things can be true at the same time.”

But she warned: “There is sadly a resignation and a consensus among parliamentarians that another MP could and possibly will be killed. Now, that’s a horrible thing to say and that’s a really blunt way of putting it, but I think that’s how people feel… There is something wrong with our political culture.”

The Labour MP also said the family needed to speak about how Jo was killed by a neo-Nazi, for her 'basic beliefs'. She explained: “We did such hard work creating a positive legacy for Jo. I actually think, as a family, we’ve been guilty of putting too brave a face on it.

‌



“Talking about how amazing Jo was - and she was bloody brilliant; talking about the kind of person she was and the values that she lived by; using the most horrific of circumstances to do something positive through the Great Get Together and all the events that we do around Jo’s birthday. What we haven’t talked about is the fact that she was murdered by a neo-Nazi with fascist, right-wing views because of her basic beliefs.”

View 5 Images Her "brilliant" sister Jo Cox who was murdered in 2016 (Image: PA)

‌



She added: “We don’t talk about that enough. One of the things I’m wrestling with is how I talk about that in a way that is, a) not too painful for me that I end up having a breakdown but, b) in a way that is helpful for the country so that we can use what happened to Jo, and some of the other dreadful things that we see happening around the country, and indeed around the world, as a way of uniting people and bringing people together. That’s a really difficult balance for me.”

She also discussed her greatest challenge, her private members’ bill on assisted dying. The historic bill has been delayed by the House of Lords after being voted through by the Commons. She explained that the issue of assisted dying "would only ever have been done through a private members’ bill because no government would put it in their manifesto."

Kim added: “I didn’t know how bad the status quo was. I didn’t know how many heartbreaking stories I would hear about people having lost loved ones in really traumatic circumstances. I didn’t really fully understand the inequity of Dignitas and Switzerland. I didn’t know the statistics around terminally ill people taking their own lives.”

‌



View 5 Images Labour MP Kim Leadbeater (centre) with Dignity in Dying campaigners as they gather in Parliament Square, central London, in support of the "assisted dying bill" (Image: PA)

She described the painful deaths people face as “total madness.", adding: “(But) I can’t walk away from something that I see as being fundamentally wrong. Jo was exactly the same. I think this is our upbringing: if we see an injustice then we would tend to run into that rather than run away from it.”

Kim stepped into her sister’s shoes five years after she was killed, in 2021, to represent Labour in Spen Valley where she and her sister had grown up. She recalled: “It was something that was thrust upon me under the most horrendous of circumstances.”

Article continues below

The former fitness lecturer and personal trainer from West Yorkshire says she thinks “it’s probably the most ridiculous job in the world.” She added: “I am the least healthy I have probably ever been in my life. Absolutely dreadful… But I can’t have worked any harder.”

“I’d be surprised if I were still an MP,” she says when asked what the next five years look like. “It’s just so draining. I mean, I have no work-life balance, so I’m not sure how sustainable that is.” Irrespective of the challenge Reform and the Greens might pose at the next general election, Leadbeater is certain that she doesn’t want to become part of the Westminster furniture.

“I’ve been on an extremely painful journey. Looking at the last 10 years and thinking about what I’ve learnt during that time, I want to be where I can make the most difference and I’ll have to make a decision at some point whether I think that is in politics or out of politics.”

News.title: Brady steps down as West Ham vice-chair
News.content:
Brady's arrival at West Ham followed more than 16 years at Birmingham City, where she was appointed managing director aged 23 in 1993. She later became the youngest managing director of a UK public limited company when she floated the club on the London Stock Exchange in 1997.

At West Ham, Brady oversaw the club's move from Upton Park to London Stadium in 2016, beating Tottenham to secure the tenancy, as well as Declan Rice's Â£105m transfer to Arsenal.

On the field, the club achieved European success, reaching the Europa League semi-finals in 2021-22 and winning the 2022-23 Conference League - their first major trophy since 1980.

West Ham have spent 14 consecutive seasons in the Premier League, but are in danger of relegation to the Championship, sitting just two points clear of 18th-placed Tottenham with five matches to play.

Some West Ham fans have frequently protested against Brady and co-owner Sullivan, including during the current season, with on-field performances and dissatisfaction with the stadium among their complaints.

Brady has also been involved in the women's team, who are 11th in the Women's Super League.

They remain the only WSL team yet to play at their club's larger men's stadium - and the women's academy is the only in the league to be ranked category two.

West Ham's joint-chair Daniel Kretinsky alluded to the opposition to Brady as he praised her work at the club.

"Her contribution to West Ham United's growth, such as the long-term contract for the London Stadium, shareholders transition and the British record transfer of Declan Rice, has been absolutely essential and not always fully appreciated," Kretinsky said.

"Karren is also very highly appreciated in the Premier League leadership community and was an excellent representative of our club there."

Joint-chair Sullivan, who also worked with Brady when he owned Birmingham City, hailed her as an "exceptional leader" and a "key figure in the club's development".

Alongside her career as a football executive, Brady has spent 16 years as Lord Alan Sugar's assistant on BBC show The Apprentice and entered the House of Lords as a life peer in 2014.

West Ham executive director Nathan Thompson has also stepped down from his role with immediate effect, saying it has been "a privilege to be a part of this club".

"I am proud to have been one of only two black board members in the Premier League, and I look forward to seeing greater diversity in leadership across the game," he added.

News.title: Seven more arrested over conspiracy to commit arson at another Jewish site in London
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

Seven more people have been arrested following a series of arson attacks on Jewish sites in London.

The Metropolitan Police said the suspects were arrested within the past 48 hours over an alleged conspiracy to commit a further arson attack, although the specific target is not yet known.

Since late March there have been arson attacks on Jewish community ambulances in Golders Green, two synagogues and a former Jewish charity, as well as an incident where a drone was flown near the Israeli embassy.

The latest arrests by detectives from Counter-Terrorism Policing London, saw three men aged 24, 25 and 26 held in Harpenden on Sunday, and on Monday a 25-year-old man arrested in Stevenage, as well as a 26-year-old man and two women aged 50 and 59 detained in a car near Birmingham.

The men arrested in Harpenden have been released on bail, while the other four remain in custody, the Metropolitan Police said.

Another arrest has also been made over the embassy incident, that saw a drone flown in Kensington Gardens carrying jars that were later found to contain non-hazardous material.

A 39-year-old man was held in Ealing under section 41 of the Terrorism Act, which allows a suspect to be arrested without a warrant if they are suspected of being a terrorist.

So far, 23 people have been arrested over the series of attacks on Jewish sites.

open image in gallery The burnt out remains of Hatzola ambulances in Golders Green (Jamie Lashmar/PA) ( PA Wire )

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, the Senior National Co-ordinator of Counter Terrorism Policing, said: “We’ve made very clear that we will be relentless in our pursuit of anyone involved in carrying out or planning these arson attacks.

“Our message is clear, we will not tolerate this intimidation of our communities, and will pursue those responsible. One of our key lines of inquiry is whether criminal proxies – that is to say people being paid money to carry out a crime, are being used to commit any of these arsons.

“While our investigations into this are still ongoing, my message to anyone even considering getting involved in this type of activity is this, the stakes are high and it is absolutely not worth the risk.

“When we identify you, we will seek to prosecute you. This will include considering offences under the National Security Act which comes with a significant sentence and lifetime restrictions.

“We will not rest until all those responsible for these acts are held to full account.

“As well as making arrests, Counter Terrorism Policing resources have also been deployed in north-west London to support the significant Met Police operation to help deter further attacks and provide reassurance to Jewish places of worship and businesses.

“I would like to thank our communities for their support as we investigate these crimes, and would urge the public to be alert to anything which doesn’t feel right and report it to us.”

News.content:

There are moments in public life when someone carefully lifts the lid to reveal what really happens in the corridors of power and show us that the gruesome details are even worse than we thought.

That was the case on Tuesday when the now-sacked chief mandarin of the Foreign Office, Sir Olly Robbins, gave evidence to to the Commons Foreign Affairs Select Committee over the Peter Mandelson vetting scandal – and revealed a Downing Street operation defined by cronyism and cynicism to its very core.

While some of what Sir Olly said was caveated, the key takeaways from his testimony damn Sir Keir Starmer and the apparent toxic culture within the inner sanctum of his government.

During a two-hour session, we learnt that there was an alleged attempt by the Cabinet Office to exclude Peter Mandelson from security vetting for the crucial role of ambassador to the US. We also learnt there were regular calls and “constant chasing” from the No 10 private office (that’s the prime minister’s private office) to push the appointment of Mandelson – a known friend of a disgraced paedophile and also a proven security risk.

Sir Olly also claimed there was a “strong expectation” that Mandelson needed to be in post – and in America – “as quickly as humanly possibly”. He said the political consequences of him overruling the decision – because the appointment had already been announced publicly – would have been catastrophic.

The former Foreign Office head also gave a damning assessment of Sir Keir’s judgement, pointing out that the prime minister was warned of the risks of Mandelson’s appointment through Cabinet Office checks and pushed it through anyway.

open image in gallery Sir Olly Robbins gives evidence in the Commons on Tuesday ( ParliamentTV )

But the cherry on the cake was an attempt by No 10 to pressure the Foreign Office into finding an ambassador’s role for Starmer’s former director of communications, Lord Matthew Doyle, at a time when top diplomats were at risk of losing their jobs under departmental restructuring.

Sir Olly revealed that not only was a man since suspended from the Labour Party because of his support for a convicted paedophile – just like Mandelson and Jeffrey Epstein – pushed for an ambassadorial role, but that he was under “strict instructions” not to tell David Lammy, the then foreign secretary, about the demand.

“I felt very uncomfortable about that,” Sir Olly told the committee, adding that he “kept giving advice that I thought this would be very hard for the office and was hard for me personally to defend”.

Lord Doyle was later made a peer. But he had the Labour whip withdrawn earlier this year after it emerged he had campaigned on behalf of a friend who had been charged with possessing indecent images of children.

What is worrying is that – while these revelations are all shocking in themselves and certainly raise further questions about the prime minister’s own probity, knowledge and general account of events – they may only be scratching the surface of the murky depths of cronyism.

open image in gallery The cronyism in Keir Starmer’s government has been exposed ( AP )

We now understand, in a way, why Downing Street did not initiate emergency investigations when The Independent revealed that Mandelson had failed security vetting in September. In a way, they knew the answer, because at the time they just wanted him appointed, according to Sir Olly’s testimony. Some in the Cabinet Office even questioned the need to vet him at all, he told MPs.

But it is the attempt to give Doyle a sensitive senior diplomatic job that may end up being the killer blow for Starmer. To appoint one friend of a paedophile as an ambassador is unfortunate, but two is unforgivable.

Then, to deliberately keep the discussions away from the foreign secretary – who would eventually have had to make such an appointment – is astounding and reveals the toxic culture in the Starmer operation, possibly more so when Morgan McSweeney was at the helm.

It all paints a picture of a small, self-serving elite – the very criticism levelled at Starmer’s government by critics on the Labour back benches.

It seems that the prime minister knew about the risks, but wanted his Labour friends to get their plum jobs anyway.

open image in gallery Downing Street exerted pressure to get Lord Matthew Doyle an ambassadorial role ( House of Lords/UK Parliament/PA )

No wonder ambitious young special advisers in the Labour government have previously made it clear to The Independent that they would consider it a bad career move to be brought into Downing Street and would rather stay in one of the outlying departments.

They do not want to be part of a setup that is toxic in nature and limping to an inevitable demise, probably in May when the election results should finish Sir Keir’s battered premiership.

What Sir Olly has revealed about Sir Keir’s inner operation is a world away from the high moral tone that the prime minister himself claimed he wanted to bring in as the culture of his government.

The questions about Starmer’s integrity and judgement have been answered in the polite and calm responses of a former senior mandarin.

But the answers are damning.
